origins.section: Any Binary in the Model Can Be the Indicator
An Indicator Constraint Reads Back, but Cannot Be Edited

recorded.prompt:q-existing-binary: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-existing-binary: Table: activate_on_zero True means 'the row holds when z = 0'. The indicator must be binary. So buy[v] = 0 implies miles[v] <= 0.

recorded.outcome:q-change-limit: 'to change a rule: delete it and add it again'. The page also says the program 'must replace its own reference'.
recorded.prompt:q-solver-choice: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-solver-choice: 'A Model for HiGHS States the Rule as a Linear Row'; 'when the data give a tight bound... the linear row runs anywhere'.

recorded.prompt:q-existing-binary:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-existing-binary:a: 'The indicator must be a binary variable... A continuous variable with the same bounds is refused.' miles is continuous.

recorded.outcome:q-existing-binary:b: Same passage: a continuous indicator is refused ('indicator variable is not binary').
